Let g be a finite dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra, and let V be a finite dimensional represenation of g. We give a closed formula for the mth Frobenius-Schur indicator, m>1, of V in representation-theoretic terms. We deduce that the indicators take integer values, and that for a large enough m, the mth indicator of V equals the dimension of the zero weight space of V. For the classical Lie algebras sl(n), so(2n), so(2n+1) and sp(2n), this is the case for m greater or equal to 2n-1, 4n-5, 4n-3 and 2n+1, respectively.

We derive a closed formula, in representation-theoretic terms, for the \(m\)th Frobenius–Schur indicator of \(V\), where \(m>1\). We show that these indicators are integer-valued and that, for sufficiently large \(m\), the \(m\)th indicator of \(V\) equals the dimension of the zero-weight space of \(V\). Let \(\mathfrak{g}\) be a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra, and let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional \(\mathfrak{g}\)-module. For every integer \(m>1\), the \(m\)th Frobenius–Schur indicator of \(V\) admits a closed formula expressed in representation-theoretic terms. This formula implies, in particular, that all Frobenius–Schur indicators are integers.

Moreover, the indicators eventually stabilize: for all sufficiently large \(m\), the \(m\)th Frobenius–Schur indicator of \(V\) is equal to the dimension of its zero-weight space \(V[0]\). Explicit bounds for this stabilization can be given for the classical simple Lie algebras. Namely, the equality
\[
\nu_m(V)=\dim V[0]
\]
holds for
\[
m\ge 2n-1 \quad\text{if }\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{sl}(n),
\]
\[
m\ge 4n-5 \quad\text{if }\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{so}(2n),
\]
\[
m\ge 4n-3 \quad\text{if }\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{so}(2n+1),
\]
and
\[
m\ge 2n+1 \quad\text{if }\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{sp}(2n).
\]
Thus, beyond these explicit thresholds, the Frobenius–Schur indicator is determined entirely by the multiplicity of the zero weight in the representation.
outputs.L4:
Let \(\mathfrak g\) be a complex semisimple Lie algebra and \(V\) a finite-dimensional \(\mathfrak g\)-module. For every integer \(m>1\), the \(m\)th Frobenius–Schur indicator of \(V\) can be expressed entirely in terms of the weights of \(V\) and the Weyl group of \(\mathfrak g\). If \(W\) is the Weyl group, \(\rho\) is the half-sum of the positive roots, and \(V[\mu]\) denotes the \(\mu\)-weight space, then
\[
\nu_m(V)
   =\sum_{w\in W}\operatorname{sgn}(w)\,
     \dim V\!\left[\frac{\rho-w\rho}{m}\right],
\]
where a summand is understood to be zero whenever \((\rho-w\rho)/m\) is not a weight of \(V\). Equivalently, \(\nu_m(V)\) is the multiplicity of the trivial representation in the \(m\)th Adams operation applied to the character of \(V\).

This formula immediately shows that all higher Frobenius–Schur indicators are integers, even though their definitions may initially present them as character-theoretic or integral quantities. It also generalizes the familiar second Frobenius–Schur indicator: for an irreducible self-dual representation, \(\nu_2(V)\) distinguishes whether the invariant bilinear form is symmetric or alternating, while it vanishes for a non-self-dual irreducible representation.

A further consequence is eventual stabilization. As \(m\) grows, the nonzero vectors \((\rho-w\rho)/m\) cease to be integral weights. Thus only the identity element \(w=1\) contributes, and the formula reduces to
\[
\nu_m(V)=\dim V[0].
\]
Hence, for sufficiently large \(m\), the \(m\)th Frobenius–Schur indicator is simply the dimension of the zero-weight space of \(V\), independently of the other weights and their multiplicities.

For the classical simple Lie algebras, uniform stabilization bounds can be given explicitly. The equality
\[
\nu_m(V)=\dim V[0]
\]
holds for every finite-dimensional representation \(V\) once
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\mathfrak g & \text{stabilization threshold}\\ \hline
\mathfrak{sl}(n) & m\ge 2n-1,\\
\mathfrak{so}(2n) & m\ge 4n-5,\\
\mathfrak{so}(2n+1) & m\ge 4n-3,\\
\mathfrak{sp}(2n) & m\ge 2n+1.
\end{array}
\]
These bounds depend only on the type and rank of the Lie algebra, not on the representation. The result therefore gives both a closed representation-theoretic formula for every higher indicator and a uniform description of its stable value.
outputs.L5:
### Lie Brackets and the Frobenius Theorem

Let \(M\) be a smooth manifold, and let \(\mathcal D\subset TM\) be a smooth distribution of constant rank. Thus, for every point \(p\in M\), the subspace \(\mathcal D_p\subset T_pM\) specifies a collection of admissible tangent directions.

The **Lie bracket** measures whether vector fields tangent to \(\mathcal D\) remain compatible with this distribution. If \(X\) and \(Y\) are smooth vector fields satisfying \(X_p,Y_p\in\mathcal D_p\), the distribution is called **involutive** when

\[
[X,Y]_p\in\mathcal D_p
\]

for every \(p\in M\). Although \(X\) and \(Y\) may individually point along the distribution, their flows need not combine to remain inside it; the Lie bracket captures precisely this infinitesimal obstruction.

The **Frobenius theorem** states that a constant-rank distribution is integrable if and only if it is involutive. Integrability means that through every point of \(M\) there exists an immersed submanifold whose tangent space at each point equals the distribution. Equivalently, near every point one can choose local coordinates

\[
(x^1,\ldots,x^n)
\]

such that \(\mathcal D\) is spanned by the coordinate vector fields

\[
\frac{\partial}{\partial x^1},\ldots,
\frac{\partial}{\partial x^k}.
\]

Hence, the Frobenius theorem provides a fundamental bridge between algebraic information encoded by Lie brackets and the geometric existence of submanifolds. It shows that a system of tangent directions comes from a family of local leaves exactly when those directions are closed under the Lie bracket.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write an abstract for a paper deriving a closed representation-theoretic formula for higher Frobenius–Schur indicators of finite-dimensional representations of complex semisimple Lie algebras.
counterfactuals.output: We derive a closed representation-theoretic formula for the higher Frobenius–Schur indicators of finite-dimensional representations of a complex semisimple Lie algebra. Passing to a compact real form, we express the \(m\)-th indicator as the Haar integral of the character evaluated on the \(m\)-th power map, or equivalently as the multiplicity of the trivial representation in the \(m\)-th Adams operation. Weyl integration and the Weyl character formula then reduce this expression to a finite sum determined by the root system, Weyl group, highest weight, and weight multiplicities of the representation. The resulting formula is uniform in the Lie algebra and in the order \(m\), applies to arbitrary finite-dimensional modules, and recovers the classical Frobenius–Schur indicator when \(m=2\). We also describe structural consequences, including integrality, additivity, duality invariance, and effective criteria for vanishing and nonvanishing. Examples in classical and exceptional types illustrate how the formula turns higher indicators into explicit computations in weight-lattice combinatorics.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the main results on the \(m\)th Frobenius–Schur indicator of a finite-dimensional representation \(V\) of a complex semisimple Lie algebra, including integrality and stabilization to the dimension of the zero-weight space.
counterfactuals.output:
Let \(\mathfrak g\) be a complex semisimple Lie algebra, \(V\) a finite-dimensional \(\mathfrak g\)-module, and \(G\) the simply connected compact group with complexified Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\). The \(m\)th Frobenius–Schur indicator is

\[
\nu_m(V)=\int_G \chi_V(g^m)\,dg,\qquad m\ge 1,
\]

with normalized Haar measure.

Choose a Cartan subalgebra, positive roots, Weyl group \(W\), and let \(\rho\) be the half-sum of the positive roots. Weyl integration gives the weight-multiplicity formula

\[
\boxed{\displaystyle
\nu_m(V)=\sum_{w\in W}(-1)^{\ell(w)}
\dim V\!\left[\frac{\rho-w\rho}{m}\right],
}
\]

where \(V[\mu]\) is the \(\mu\)-weight space, interpreted as \(0\) if \((\rho-w\rho)/m\) is not a weight of \(V\).

Consequences:

- **Integrality:**  
  \[
  \nu_m(V)\in \mathbb Z
  \]
  for every \(m\ge 1\). Equivalently, \(\nu_m(V)\) is the multiplicity of the trivial representation in the \(m\)th Adams operation \(\psi^m(V)\), viewed as a virtual representation.

- **Classical case \(m=2\):** \(\nu_2(V)\) recovers the usual Frobenius–Schur behavior: for an irreducible \(V\), it is \(1\), \(-1\), or \(0\) according as \(V\) carries an invariant symmetric form, an invariant alternating form, or is not self-dual.

- **Eventual stabilization:** Since the set
  \[
  \{\rho-w\rho:w\in W\}
  \]
  is finite, for all sufficiently large \(m\) the equality
  \[
  m\mu=\rho-w\rho
  \]
  cannot hold for a nonzero weight \(\mu\) of \(V\). Thus only \(w=1\), for which \(\rho-w\rho=0\), contributes. Therefore
  \[
  \boxed{\displaystyle
  \nu_m(V)=\dim V[0]\qquad\text{for all sufficiently large }m.
  }
  \]

In particular, the sequence of higher indicators is eventually constant and nonnegative; its stable value is exactly the multiplicity of the zero weight in \(V\). If \(V\) has no zero weight, then \(\nu_m(V)=0\) for all sufficiently large \(m\).
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: State a theorem-style research summary giving the stabilization bounds for higher Frobenius–Schur indicators in the classical cases \(\mathfrak{sl}(n)\), \(\mathfrak{so}(2n)\), \(\mathfrak{so}(2n+1)\), and \(\mathfrak{sp}(2n)\).
counterfactuals.output:
**Theorem (uniform stabilization of higher Frobenius–Schur indicators).**  
Let \(\mathfrak g\) be a complex simple Lie algebra, \(V\) a finite-dimensional \(\mathfrak g\)-module, and
\[
\nu_m(V)
=
\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(c_m\mid (V^{\otimes m})^{\mathfrak g}\right),
\]
where \(c_m=(1\,2\,\dots ,m)\) acts by cyclic permutation of tensor factors. Equivalently, for a compact form \(G\),
\[
\nu_m(V)=\int_G \chi_V(g^m)\,dg .
\]

If \(h\) denotes the Coxeter number of \(\mathfrak g\), then
\[
\boxed{\nu_m(V)=\dim V[0]\qquad\text{for every }m\ge 2h-1,}
\]
where \(V[0]\) is the zero-weight space of \(V\). Thus the indicator sequence stabilizes uniformly—independently of \(V\)—to the zero-weight multiplicity.

For the classical families this gives:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\mathfrak g & h & \text{stabilization bound}\\ \hline
\mathfrak{sl}(n)\;(A_{n-1}) & n
  & m\ge 2n-1,\\[2mm]
\mathfrak{so}(2n)\;(D_n) & 2n-2
  & m\ge 4n-5,\\[2mm]
\mathfrak{so}(2n+1)\;(B_n) & 2n
  & m\ge 4n-1,\\[2mm]
\mathfrak{sp}(2n)\;(C_n) & 2n
  & m\ge 4n-1.
\end{array}
\]

In particular, throughout these stable ranges the higher indicators are nonnegative integers and depend only on the multiplicity of the zero weight in \(V\). These are uniform sufficient bounds; individual modules may stabilize earlier.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a concise mathematical abstract explaining that higher Frobenius–Schur indicators are integers and eventually equal the dimension of \(V\)'s zero-weight space, with explicit bounds for all classical Lie algebras.
counterfactuals.output:
**Abstract.** Let \(K\) be a compact, connected, simply connected classical Lie group, and let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional \(K\)-module with character \(\chi_V\). For \(m\ge1\), define the \(m\)-th Frobenius–Schur indicator by
\[
\nu_m(V)=\int_K \chi_V(g^m)\,dg .
\]
Using the Weyl integration formula, we obtain
\[
\nu_m(V)=\sum_{w\in W}\det(w)\,
\dim V\!\left[\frac{\rho-w\rho}{m}\right],
\]
where \(W\) is the Weyl group, \(\rho\) is the half-sum of positive roots, and a nonintegral weight contributes zero. This formula shows directly that every higher indicator is an integer. Moreover, if \(h\) is the Coxeter number, then for \(m>h\) all terms with \(w\neq1\) vanish, so
\[
\nu_m(V)=\dim V[0].
\]
Thus stabilization holds uniformly for
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\mathfrak g & \text{sufficient bound}\\ \hline
A_r & m\ge r+2,\\
B_r & m\ge 2r+1,\\
C_r & m\ge 2r+1,\\
D_r & m\ge 2r-1.
\end{array}
\]
Hence, for every classical Lie algebra, higher Frobenius–Schur indicators are integral and eventually recover the multiplicity of the zero weight, with bounds depending only on the root system and not on \(V\).
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: What are the principal results concerning the \(m\)th Frobenius–Schur indicator, for \(m>1\), of a finite-dimensional representation of a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra?
counterfactuals.output:
Let \(\mathfrak g\) be a complex semisimple Lie algebra and \(V\) a finite-dimensional \(\mathfrak g\)-module. For \(m>1\), the \(m\)th Frobenius–Schur indicator is defined by  
\[
\nu_m(V)=\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(c_m\mid (V^{\otimes m})^{\mathfrak g}\right),
\]
where
\[
c_m(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_m)
   =v_2\otimes\cdots\otimes v_m\otimes v_1.
\]

The main results are as follows.

### 1. Compact-group and Adams-operation descriptions

If \(K\) is the simply connected compact group with complexified Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\), and \(\chi_V\) is the character of \(V\), then
\[
\boxed{\nu_m(V)=\int_K\chi_V(k^m)\,dk.}
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\nu_m(V)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}_K\!\left(\mathbf 1,\psi^m(V)\right),
\]
where \(\psi^m\) is the \(m\)th Adams operation on the representation ring; here the right side is interpreted as the multiplicity in the corresponding virtual representation.

### 2. Weyl-group formula

Fix a Cartan subalgebra, a set of positive roots, Weyl group \(W\), and
\[
\rho=\frac12\sum_{\alpha>0}\alpha.
\]
Writing \(V[\mu]\) for the \(\mu\)-weight space, one has
\[
\boxed{\displaystyle
\nu_m(V)=\sum_{w\in W}(-1)^{\ell(w)}
   \dim V\!\left[\frac{\rho-w\rho}{m}\right],
}
\]
with a summand understood to be zero unless \((\rho-w\rho)/m\) is a weight of \(V\). This is the basic computational formula.

Consequently, every \(\nu_m(V)\) is an integer, even though it is initially defined as the trace of an operator of finite order.

### 3. The case \(m=2\)

For an irreducible \(V\), the usual Frobenius–Schur trichotomy is recovered:
\[
\nu_2(V)=
\begin{cases}
 1,&V\text{ admits a nondegenerate invariant symmetric form},\\
-1,&V\text{{ admits a nondegenerate invariant alternating form}},\\
 0,&V\not\cong V^*.
\end{cases}
\]

Thus \(\nu_2\) detects whether an irreducible representation is orthogonal, symplectic, or non-self-dual.

### 4. Higher indicators are nonnegative

A principal feature peculiar to the connected semisimple setting is that
\[
\boxed{\nu_m(V)\ge 0\qquad (m\ge 3).}
\]
Hence the negative value occurring for symplectic representations at \(m=2\) does not occur for higher indicators. Higher indicators need not be only \(0\) or \(1\); they can be larger.

### 5. Stabilization

For fixed \(V\), only finitely many \(m\) allow a nonidentity Weyl-group term in the formula above. Therefore
\[
\boxed{\nu_m(V)=\dim V[0]\quad\text{for all sufficiently large }m.}
\]
Thus, unlike the indicators of finite groups, which are typically periodic in \(m\), indicators for semisimple Lie algebras eventually stabilize at the multiplicity of the zero weight.

For example, for the irreducible \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\)-module \(V_n\) of highest weight \(n\),
\[
\nu_2(V_n)=(-1)^n,
\qquad
\nu_m(V_n)=
\begin{cases}
1,&n\ \text{even},\\
0,&n\ \text{odd},
\end{cases}
\quad m\ge3.
\]

In short, the central results are the compact-group integral, the explicit Weyl-group/weight-multiplicity formula, integrality and nonnegativity for \(m\ge3\), recovery of the classical \(m=2\) criterion, and eventual stabilization to the zero-weight multiplicity.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
